questions.question: Alcohol impairment starts:

options.text: At about half the legal alcohol limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your riding ability. You can be impaired below the legal limit. Never drink before riding.

questions.question: A rectangular sign shows:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show traffic rules like speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. Follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: Your best source for motorcycle information is:
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual has information about your specific motorcycle. It covers how to operate it and when to maintain it.

questions.question: An integrated braking system:

options.text: Applies some rear braking when you use the front brake.
Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both wheels when either brake is used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking when you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's brake system.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce speed.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up or brake hard during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, hold the handlebars tight, slowly reduce speed, lean forward, and pull over safely.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot. Lift your foot to shift up. Push down to shift down.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used in curves.
Should use the road shoulder in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than regular two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: A passenger should:

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you during turns. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control, and hold onto handholds or your waist.

questions.question: A flat rear tire is shown by:

options.text: A hissing sound from the rear.
The back jerking side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back jerking side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You usually won't hear the tire fail.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake on wet roads.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: What happens when a rear tire skids?

options.text: You cannot steer or change direction.
It is only dangerous if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot steer or change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a crash with serious injury or death. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When this happens, you lose the ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you stay out of other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, protects your lane, shows other drivers your intentions, helps you avoid wind blasts, and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: Rain suits:

options.text: Should not puff up or balloon when riding.
Are not needed because motorcycles cannot ride in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not puff up or balloon when riding.
questions.explanation: Good rain suits made for motorcycle riding will not tear or balloon when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Pre-ride checks only by a mechanic.

questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle more often than a car. Do a complete check before every ride.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.explanation: THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) is the main active ingredient in marijuana.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Losing grip on one or both wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose grip on one or both wheels and crash.
